Market today: The tech sector is seeing mixed signals. Software names like ServiceNow are rallying, but the chip space is a bit of a tug-of-war with Marvell up on a Google deal while Broadcom dips. Underlying this, macro concerns about Fed rates and the ballooning national debt continue to loom, which can hit growth-focused tech hard.

Your holdings: SOXL (-52.56%) and SPAL (-40%) are your biggest concerns. Both are leveraged ETFs, meaning they decay over time and their deep drawdowns are amplified by your margin use. SMH (-11.86%) and QQQI (-3.67%) are also flagged for trimming, with their stops relatively close.

Watch: Keep a very close eye on the stops for SOXL and SPAL. Given their leveraged nature and significant losses, respecting those levels is critical to prevent further capital erosion. Also, monitor broader chip sector sentiment.

Bottom line: With significant exposure to leveraged products and margin, aggressive risk management and stop discipline are paramount right now.
plays: SOXL is down over 50% and leveraged; consider trimming aggressively or tightening its stop from 200 to protect capital.
SPAL, another leveraged ETF, is down 40%; strictly respect its 21.38 stop to prevent further amplified losses.
ASML has a scanner BUY setup at 1749.98-1748.23 with a stop at 1744.51, aligning with your chip focus.
